Users who rely on encrypted HFS+ drives will no longer need to decrypt them before converting to APFS, making them compatible with macOS 28. Here's what this change means.

Apple has updated its migration guidance for encrypted HFS+ drives in macOS 28.

A few weeks ago, Apple published a support document explaining that starting with macOS 28, "the Mac OS Extended file system format will only be used for unencrypted volumes (disks and other storage devices)."

Basically, this means that users currently relying on encrypted HFS+ external drives or other encrypted legacy Mac-formatted volumes will need to "decrypt or reformat all encrypted Mac OS Extended volumes," Apple explained.

Previously, the support page provided step-by-step instructions on how to decrypt the volume, or erase and reformat it using APFS.

Apple has now updated the page to include a third option, allowing users to convert encrypted HFS+ volumes directly to encrypted APFS without first decrypting them. Apple has now provided the following new procedure:

Convert the volume to encrypted APFS

However, Apple notes that "this solution does not apply to encrypted Time Machine backup disks."

Apple has also removed the previous instructions, including steps such as decrypting the volume first, converting to APFS without erasing it, and then optionally re-encrypting.

To view the updated support page, please follow this link.

Will this new option make it easier for you to prepare your drives for macOS 28? Let us know in the comments section.
